title: Ethical banking, fossil-free and green ranking
license: ODbL-1.0 data snapshot; CC BY-SA 4.0 explanatory text
purpose: A self-contained, re-runnable citation bundle for the reviewer question: which banking options rank highest when green financing is weighted heavily?

lensAssumptions.label: Ethical banking
lensAssumptions.valueFrame: Values-relative ranking, not a universal verdict.
lensAssumptions.disclaimer: Banking comparisons are general information, not financial advice.
lensAssumptions.caveat: The bundle freezes a source lens and query so the result can be rerun. Later live data may differ.

query.focus: Show how the banking lens ranks when green financing and ethics are the strongest weights.

meta.label: Ethical banking
meta.attribution: Where your money sleeps is one of the biggest votes it casts. Fossil-financing figures are from the Banking on Climate Chaos (BOCC) reports by Rainforest Action Network et al.; structure & certifications from the banks, GABV, B Lab and public filings. Each rating links its source and date — not financial advice. Reviewed 2026-06. Dispute or correct any rating via Contribute.

products.name: Triodos Bank
products.description: A European sustainability bank that lends only to social, cultural and environmental projects — and publishes every organisation it finances.

environment.note: Lends nothing to fossil fuels; first bank in the world to sign the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty

ethics.note: Certified B Corp and GABV co-founder; ownership mission-locked via the SAAT foundation (no holder above 10%)

transparency.note: Publishes every loan and investment it makes

provenance.fees: Monthly account fee on the current account
provenance.accessibility: UK & several EU countries; app + online, limited branches. (Note: investor depository-receipts had a 2020–23 liquidity freeze.)

products.name: GLS Bank
products.description: Germany's pioneering social-ecological bank — a member-owned cooperative that finances renewable energy, organic farming and social projects.

environment.note: Finances renewables and social projects, not fossil fuels; GABV signatory to the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty

ethics.note: A registered cooperative (member-owned) and 2009 co-founder of the Global Alliance for Banking on Values

transparency.note: Reports where members' money is lent — publishes its lending in the bank's own customer magazine

products.name: Beneficial State Bank
products.description: A West-Coast community bank majority-owned by a nonprofit foundation, so its economic rights are held in the public interest rather than by private shareholders.

environment.note: Pledged fossil-fuel-free; no lending to fossil fuels, private prisons or weapons; endorsed the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty

ethics.note: Certified B Corp, GABV member and US-Treasury-certified CDFI; majority-owned by the nonprofit Beneficial State Foundation

transparency.note: Publishes impact reporting; the nonprofit-foundation ownership model is public

products.name: Climate First Bank
products.description: A Florida-based, fully digital community bank built around climate — fossil-fuel-free and a major financier of residential solar.

environment.note: Fossil-fuel-free; financed $427M+ in residential solar since 2021, net-zero operations

ethics.note: Certified B Corp and 1% for the Planet member (GABV membership is planned, not yet confirmed)

transparency.note: Publishes impact metrics on its public impact page

products.name: Amalgamated Bank
products.description: A century-old, labour-rooted US bank — the largest B-Corp bank in America — that runs a 100% fossil-fuel-free lending portfolio.

environment.note: 100% fossil-fuel-free portfolio; ~a third of lending directed to climate solutions

ethics.note: Certified B Corp and GABV member, labour/union-rooted — though publicly listed (Nasdaq: AMAL), not a cooperative

transparency.note: Publishes impact reports; publicly listed, so filings are public

products.name: Tomorrow
products.description: A German mobile-first banking provider whose deposits are channelled into climate and impact projects.

environment.note: Deposits fund climate projects; no fossil-fuel lending

ethics.note: Sustainability-first mission; a fintech operating on a partner-bank licence (Solaris), not a licensed bank itself

transparency.note: Shows the impact of your money in-app and on its public impact page

products.name: The Co-operative Bank
products.description: A UK bank with a customer-led Ethical Policy since 1992 — and, since January 2025, back inside the mutual sector via Coventry Building Society.

environment.note: Customer-led Ethical Policy excludes fossil-fuel extraction; markets itself as fossil-free certified

ethics.note: Acquired by Coventry Building Society (completed Jan 2025), returning it to mutual ownership after hedge-fund ownership 2017–24

transparency.note: Publishes its customer-polled Ethical Policy in full

products.name: Nationwide Building Society
products.description: The world's largest building society — owned by its ~16 million members, with no shareholders and no stock-market listing.

environment.note: Does not lend to the fossil-fuel sector; named among UK institutions not financing fossil-fuel expansion

ethics.note: A member-owned mutual — no shareholders, no stock-market listing

transparency.note: Member-governed with AGM voting; climate/financed-emissions disclosure tracked publicly

products.name: Local credit union
products.description: Not-for-profit financial cooperatives owned by their members — one member, one vote — that by structure rarely finance fossil fuels.

environment.note: Structurally minimal: US credit unions can't invest in stock markets and are largely absent from fossil-financing tables — but individual unions vary, so check yours

ethics.note: Not-for-profit, member-owned cooperatives; surplus returned to members, not external shareholders

transparency.note: Member-governed (one member, one vote) by structure; disclosure practice varies by individual union

products.name: Monzo
products.description: A popular UK app-only bank. Fossil-free largely by virtue of its deposit model — but profit-driven and VC-backed, it avoids harm rather than actively funding the transition.

environment.note: States it does not lend to or invest in fossil-fuel, arms or tobacco companies; most deposits sit at the central bank

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned, VC-backed; net-zero-by-2030 aim but no positive green-finance mandate

transparency.note: Publishes business-practice notes; no financed-emissions detail

provenance.fees: Free everyday banking; paid tiers optional

products.name: Starling Bank
products.description: A UK app bank with an ethics statement excluding harmful sectors and renewable-powered operations — though, like Monzo, privately held and profit-driven.

environment.note: Ethics statement excludes fossil-fuel lending/investment; branchless with renewable-powered offices

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned, privately held; board-level climate governance but doesn't disclose financed emissions

transparency.note: Clear fees; limited impact disclosure beyond the ethics statement

products.name: bunq
products.description: A pan-European app bank that plants trees with spending and avoids fossil-fuel lending — greener than mainstream, lighter on disclosure.

environment.note: No fossil-fuel lending; plants trees with card spending

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned fintech (founder-controlled); greener than mainstream, no positive mandate

transparency.note: Limited impact disclosure — the sustainability page is the extent of it

products.name: Chime
products.description: A fee-light US banking app. It runs on partner banks and publishes no fossil-free policy or financing data, so its impact is largely unknown.

environment.note: Not a stated focus; operates on partner banks (The Bancorp, Stride) — no fossil-free policy or financing disclosure (data unavailable)

ethics.note: Mainstream, fee-free consumer model; shareholder-owned (publicly listed 2025)

transparency.note: Limited disclosure of where deposits are held beyond naming its partner banks

products.name: U.S. Bank
products.description: A large US bank — a second-tier (not top-four) fossil financier with rising fossil lending and no exclusion policy.

environment.note: About $12.8bn fossil-fuel financing in 2023 and rising; a $50bn environmental-finance goal but no fossil exclusion

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: USB); no fossil exclusion policy

transparency.note: Discloses financials (public filings); limited financed-emissions detail

products.name: Capital One
products.description: A US card-and-consumer bank. Not a flagged major fossil financier, but with no published climate or exclusion commitments.

environment.note: Not among BOCC's highlighted fossil financiers (business concentrated in cards/consumer lending) — but no fossil-free policy and limited public data

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: COF); no published climate commitments

transparency.note: Discloses financials (public filings)

products.name: Ally Bank
products.description: A branchless US bank, mostly auto finance and deposits. Not a major fossil lender, but with thin climate disclosure and no exclusion policy.

environment.note: Not a flagged major fossil financier, but sets no science-based targets, doesn't disclose financed emissions, and has no fossil-exclusion policy

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: ALLY); 'neutral by default'

transparency.note: Limited climate disclosure — no financed-emissions reporting or science-based targets

products.name: Lloyds Banking Group
products.description: A big UK high-street bank — among the lower fossil financiers of the UK majors, but still a conventional shareholder bank with no fossil-free guarantee.

environment.note: About $1.6bn fossil-fuel financing in 2024 — materially lower than Barclays/HSBC, reflecting earlier oil-and-gas restrictions

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (LSE: LLOY); mainstream

transparency.note: Discloses financials and climate reporting (public filings)

products.name: NatWest Group
products.description: A major UK high-street bank — one of the lower-financing UK majors, but a mainstream shareholder bank without a fossil-free commitment.

environment.note: About $2.7bn fossil-fuel financing in 2024 — among the lowest of the UK majors

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (LSE: NWG); mainstream

transparency.note: Discloses financials and climate reporting (public filings)

products.name: Santander UK
products.description: The UK arm of Banco Santander, whose group fossil financing is significant and rising — so it doesn't stand out as climate-aligned.

environment.note: Parent group Santander financed roughly $14–17bn in fossil fuels in 2024 and doubled its fossil debt financing vs 2021 (group-level; no separate UK figure)

ethics.note: Part of publicly traded Banco Santander; mainstream

transparency.note: Discloses financials (public filings of the listed parent group)

provenance.fees: Some accounts charge a monthly fee

products.name: HSBC
products.description: A major global bank that financed billions in fossil fuels and increased that lending into 2025 — not a values-aligned choice on climate.

environment.note: About $16.2bn fossil-fuel financing in 2024, and increased fossil financing ~16% in 2025

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (LSE: HSBA); withdrew from the Net-Zero Banking Alliance in 2025

transparency.note: Discloses financials (LSE-listed public filings)

products.name: Barclays
products.description: Europe's single largest fossil-fuel financier — a clear avoid for a climate-minded customer.

environment.note: Europe's largest fossil-fuel financier — about $35.4bn in 2024

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (LSE: BARC); withdrew from the Net-Zero Banking Alliance in 2025; criticised for 'sustainable finance' greenwashing

transparency.note: Discloses financials (LSE-listed public filings)

products.name: Wells Fargo
products.description: A top-five lifetime fossil financier that also publicly walked back its climate targets — a poor fit for climate-conscious customers.

environment.note: ~$296bn fossil-fuel financing since 2016 — the world's 5th-largest funder

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: WFC); became the first major US bank to abandon its net-zero commitment (Feb 2025); history of consumer scandals

transparency.note: Discloses financials (NYSE-listed public filings)

products.name: Citibank
products.description: A top-two lifetime fossil financier and the single biggest backer of fossil-fuel expansion since Paris — among the least climate-aligned options.

environment.note: ~$396bn fossil-fuel financing since 2016 (#2 globally) and the worst funder of fossil-fuel expansion

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: C); exited the Net-Zero Banking Alliance in 2025

transparency.note: Discloses financials (NYSE-listed public filings)

products.name: Bank of America
products.description: Consistently a top-three global fossil financier — not a values-aligned choice on climate.

environment.note: About $47bn fossil-fuel financing in 2025 (#2 globally); ~$333bn since 2016

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: BAC); exited the Net-Zero Banking Alliance in 2025

transparency.note: Discloses financials (NYSE-listed public filings)

products.name: JPMorgan Chase
products.description: The world's single largest funder of fossil fuels for most years on record — a clear avoid for a climate-minded customer.

environment.note: World's #1 fossil-fuel financier — about $58bn in 2025 (up 12.6%), and ~$430bn since 2016

ethics.note: Shareholder-owned (NYSE: JPM); exited the Net-Zero Banking Alliance in 2025; no fossil exclusion

transparency.note: Discloses financials (NYSE-listed public filings); no financed-emissions transparency

provenance.fees: Monthly account fees common unless waived
provenance.accessibility: US/global; the largest branch & ATM network, strong app
